tickets.title: Stop foreign-key and keystore failures from quarantining the brain index: ownership stamp plus decrypt-failure taxonomy
tickets.summary: quarantineUnusableIndex renames any index.json that fails to decrypt, so a process holding a different key (a test worker, another device on a shared .brain) resets the owner's ledger and forces a full re-ingest, which feeds the heavy-machine loop. Stamp a plaintext index.owner.json with the existing installId on every successful writeIndex, and classify decrypt failures as unparseable, foreign-key or keystore-unavailable. Only an unparseable index owned by this install (or unowned, for backward compatibility) is quarantined; everything else stays byte-identical and opens read-only for the session.
acceptance: writeIndex stamps .brain/index.owner.json {installId, updatedAt} (no content) after each successful write

Own or unowned plus unparseable keeps today's rename behaviour; new quarantine snapshots are capped at 5; the existing 180 index.corrupt-* files are never deleted by the app
Correlation note records quarantine timestamps against known test-run windows (metadata only, owner-approved) to close CRITIC-INV-2
Three ownership cases plus the backward-compatible case are covered in mqa-175-brain-index-poison.test.ts

When the ledger opens read-only (foreign-key or keystore-unavailable), the index is flagged unavailable so the scheduler suspends backfill, ingest, consolidation and the intelligence catch-up (deferredReason ledger_unavailable) instead of re-extracting every meeting against the empty in-memory index; data health shows the state
